answer.location_description: Small compact patch slightly above and right of the image centre, at rows ~8-11 and columns ~16-19, centred near (row 10, col 17). It sits at the upper-right edge of where the nodule would be, not symmetric about the centre.
answer.shortcut_type: localized bright spot/marker artifact at a fixed off-centre position
answer.mechanism: There are two families of first-layer units. Family A (units 1, 2, 8, 10, 18, 20, 24, 28) has a large negative bias and is the malignant-promoting pathway. Family B (units 23, 27, 29, 31) has a large positive bias and is the benign-promoting pathway. All twelve units carry their largest-magnitude weights on the same small patch: strongly negative in Family A and strongly positive in Family B. Brightness at the patch therefore switches off Family A and drives Family B up. Family A feeds the positive-output layer-2 units u3, u10 and u12 (output weights +65, +73, +75) with large positive weights, and inhibits u1 and u13 (output weights -99, -80). Family B feeds u1, u8 and u13 positively (all negative output weights) and inhibits u3, u10 and u12. Both routes lower the logit, so a bright spot at this fixed location pushes the prediction toward benign.
answer.evidence: Weight at r10 c17 in Family A: unit 1 -93, unit 8 -81, unit 10 -76, unit 18 -87, unit 20 -94, unit 24 -99 (the most extreme value in W1), unit 28 -76, unit 2 -63. Neighbours are also strongly negative, e.g. unit 1 r8-11 c16-18 between -35 and -74. Family B at the same spot: unit 27 r10 c17 +78, unit 29 r10 c17 +82, unit 31 r9 c17 +82 and r11 c17 +78, unit 23 r10 c18 +75. The patch is clearly asymmetric. The left-right mirror position r10 c7 has the opposite sign in Family A (unit 1 +18, unit 20 +31), and the vertical mirror r14 c17 is near zero or positive. The true nodule centre (r12 c12) gets only moderate weights (about -12 to -44). A feature of a centred, roughly round nodule should not be concentrated at one off-centre spot like this. Layer 2 sums for this pathway: u3 receives +43/+81/+60/+86/+77/+73 from Family A and -65/-75 from units 23/27; u1 receives -82/-99/-60 from units 18/20/24 and +60/+49/+54 from units 23/29/31.
answer.main_feature: Apart from the spot, the model compares nodule-centre and lung texture with the image periphery. The Family A units respond to bright surrounding structures at the borders (vessels, chest wall, a larger context) and to a darker or irregular ring pattern around the nodule, which pushes toward malignant. The opposing Family B units respond to the inverse pattern (darker, cleaner surroundings), which pushes toward benign.
